ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, and UBOs (25% or more) against the FINTRAC PEP list, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU/UK sanctions lists, and Canadian domestic sanctions (Special Economic Measures Act); enhanced due diligence required for PEP status, high-risk jurisdictions, or SWIFT/US-dollar wire payment rails; screening must be repeated at formation, annually, and upon any ownership or material change, with records retained for at least five years per PCMLTFA and FINTRAC Guidance 220.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized service providers - https://www.albertacorporateregistry.ca; NUANS pre-approved name search report required for corporate general partner and recommended for the Limited Partnership
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The LP name may be in English or French; a non-Roman script name requires a transliteration and a clear English or French form; the name must include 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'LP', 'Société en commandite', or 'S.E.C.'; all registered documents must be filed in English or French
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Clinic / Medical / Dental (requires prior approval from the Alberta Dental Association and College or other professional regulator)
Canadian (unless the entity is incorporated or registered under an Act of Canada)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies through the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days, attaching the NUANS report, the proposed name, and a sworn affidavit demonstrating distinctiveness and non-confusion; if reconsideration is refused, apply for judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 30 days of the refusal. A fresh NUANS report may be purchased (CAD 20-40) to resubmit a revised name. Name search reports may be renewed for one additional 90-day period if filed before expiry; no statutory extension exists for a reserved corporate name beyond the renewal period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only for the registered-office address using a licensed corporate-services provider (physical street address, not a post office box); operational premises must be a physical, appropriately zoned industrial site to satisfy the Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL), ISO 13485 quality management, municipal fire and zoning bylaws, and provincial occupational health and safety requirements
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: estimated 55-70% probability per fiscal year of an unannounced or short-notice inspection by Health Canada (Medical Devices Bureau), Alberta Occupational Health and Safety, municipal fire or building code officers, or FINTRAC AML/CFT examiners once bank wire facilities are active; ISO 13485 audits are typically announced but may be short-notice

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, including the limited partnership provisions in Part 3, sections 51-69, together with applicable regulations and the Business Corporations Act provisions where relevant to corporate partners.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Alberta Corporate Registry, accessed through an authorized registry agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership, together with the prescribed registration statement and Alberta business-name registration, if a business name is used.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an Alberta limited partnership. The partnership agreement should specify capital commitments and contribution mechanics. Alberta does not generally require formation capital to be deposited into an escrow account; contributed funds should be deposited into the partnership bank account after registration, subject to banking, beneficial-ownership, and source-of-funds checks.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Limited Partnership has no statutory board of directors. The general partner therefore adopts the following initial partner resolution: resolved that the Partnership Agreement and Declaration of Limited Partnership are approved and that each partner shall subscribe for and contribute the capital stated therein. Resolved that the registered office and records office specified in the filing are adopted. Resolved that the general partner is authorized to open bank accounts, execute formation and licensing documents, and appoint the Partnership’s authorized signatory, compliance officer, plant manager, and financial officer, subject to applicable law and the Partnership Agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Determine Partner Structure and Prepare the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Alberta Corporate Registry requirements; no pre-clearance filing is normally required for the agreement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Identify at least one general partner and one limited partner. Confirm legal names, addresses, contribution commitments, profit allocations, authority limits, withdrawal provisions, indemnities, and registered-office details. If a corporation is the general partner, complete its own corporate authorization and beneficial-ownership review. Execute the agreement in accordance with the governing law. Notarization is not normally required for Alberta execution, but foreign signatures and corporate authorizations should be notarized or certified where required by the registry agent or financial institution.
required_dossiers: Partner legal names, addresses, and ownership information
General partner certificate of incorporation and authorizing resolution, if applicable
Registered office and records office information
Proposed Alberta business name, if different from the legal partnership name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct incomplete ownership, address, authority, or name information before filing. Obtain a legal-name reservation or amend the proposed business name if the registry agent identifies a conflict or prohibited name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized Alberta registry agent or an approved registry service channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed Declaration of Limited Partnership and associated registration information, including the partnership name, general-partner details, registered office, records office, and prescribed declaration particulars. Pay the applicable registry and service-agent fees. Obtain the Certificate of Registration and registry profile. Confirm that the registered office is physically located in Alberta and that statutory records can be maintained there. Foreign-executed documents should be certified and, where applicable, accompanied by an English translation.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement or confirmation of its execution
General partner identification and corporate authority documents
Registered office and records office confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the registry agent to any rejected or queried filing, correct the prescribed form, replace an unavailable name, and resubmit. Preserve the rejection notice and corrected filing for the statutory records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Governance, Records, and Banking Controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry for registered information; the partnership’s selected Canadian financial institution for account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the initial partner resolution, maintain the executed partnership agreement and registration certificate, establish accounting and tax records, and document signing authorities. Open a Canadian partnership bank account after registration. Complete beneficial-ownership, sanctions, source-of-funds, and tax-residency questionnaires. Establish separate books for partner contributions, distributions, manufacturing costs, inventory, and intercompany charges. Do not represent the limited partnership as having directors unless a separate corporate general partner has directors.
required_dossiers: Accounting chart of accounts and records-retention policy
Intercompany services, financing, or intellectual-property agreements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure bank onboarding deficiencies by providing certified identity, ownership charts, source-of-funds evidence, tax forms, and corporate authority documents. Amend signing mandates by written partner or general-partner resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Federal and Alberta Tax and Employment Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance; Workers’ Compensation Board of Alberta; Alberta Employment Standards and applicable municipal authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Business Number and register for GST/HST where required or commercially appropriate. Register payroll accounts before paying employees and assess corporate-income-tax filing obligations of the general partner and partnership information-return obligations. Register with the Workers’ Compensation Board of Alberta before commencing covered employment. Confirm municipal business licensing, land-use, building, and occupancy requirements for the manufacturing premises.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration and partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct account-registration data, file missing returns, pay assessed amounts and interest, and request administrative reconsideration or objection where a registration or assessment is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Manufacturing, Medical-Device, Environmental, and Premises Approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Health Canada; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety; the applicable municipality, fire authority, and building authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Classify the zirconia blocks and milling discs under the federal medical-device framework based on intended use, claims, design, and supply-chain role. Obtain any required medical-device establishment or device licence before importing, distributing, or marketing. Screen the facility under Alberta environmental legislation and obtain any required approval, registration, authorization, or municipal trade-waste consent. Secure development, building, occupancy, fire, electrical, and occupational-safety clearances before production.
required_dossiers: Technical file, quality-system evidence, labeling, and claims substantiation
Health Canada licence application, if required
Environmental screening and emissions or wastewater inventory
Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act approval or registration, if required
Building, occupancy, fire, and electrical inspection records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to technical or environmental information requests within the stated deadline, submit revised drawings or controls, request reconsideration of a licensing decision where available, and do not commence the affected activity until the required authorization is issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada, Medical Devices Directorate, for regulated dental medical-device activities; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas and the applicable municipality for environmental and premises approvals. Alberta has no single general provincial manufacturing licence for this activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence or device licence, as applicable under the federal Food and Drugs Act and Medical Devices Regulations; Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act approval, registration, or authorization where the facility’s emissions, wastewater, waste, or activities trigger a provincial requirement.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific environmental screening; normally no standalone full EIA for a standard small or medium dental-ceramic manufacturing facility unless triggered by project scale, location, emissions, water use, waste profile, or another prescribed activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Meet all conditions in applicable Alberta approvals and municipal wastewater bylaws. Control particulate matter, silica-containing dust, VOCs, furnace or kiln emissions, and process wastewater using documented engineering controls and monitoring. Characterize ceramic powders, contaminated filters, solvents, sludges, and other residues under Alberta waste requirements; use approved carriers and facilities for regulated waste. No universal numeric threshold should be assumed without a site-specific approval and process inventory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal development, building, occupancy, fire-prevention, and emergency-access approvals. Complete fire-alarm, suppression, hazardous-material storage, electrical, ventilation, pressure-equipment, and structural-load inspections as applicable. Implement Alberta Occupational Health and Safety compliance, hazard assessments, worker training, machine guarding, respiratory and silica controls, chemical handling, incident reporting, and workplace emergency procedures before commissioning the plant.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Federal Tax Authority with Provincial Coordination for Alberta
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident Limited Partnerships register for a Business Number (BN) via CRA My Business portal or Form RC59. Requires foreign partnership agreement, proof of non-residency, and GST supply indication. Processing: 5-10 business days. Separate income tax registration if carrying on business in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available. Partnerships default to pass-through taxation at partner level. Hybrid mismatch relief limited to GAAR provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD annual taxable supplies in Canada
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: GST/HST registrants issue compliant tax invoices. Most file GST returns electronically via CRA My Business portal. No real-time digital stamping or clearance; self-assessment with audit verification required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for exports of goods (including dental ceramic blocks) and offshore services. Requires proof goods/services left Canada and did not enter domestic market.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Insufficient documentation triggers GST reassessment, penalties up to 50% of evaded tax, and criminal prosecution for fraudulent zero-rating claims. Input tax credits clawed back retroactively.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential bank supervision and FINTRAC for AML/CTF enforcement; no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration exists in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) enjoys full current and capital account convertibility; Canada abolished statutory exchange controls under the Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1951. No government authorization, central bank approval, or currency license is required for cross-border capital injections into an Alberta Limited Partnership (CA_LP), distribution of profits, or repatriation of capital. Non-resident limited partners may receive profit distributions and capital returns in CAD or foreign currency without any convertibility ceiling, provided the transaction is not structured to evade the Income Tax Act (ITA) Part XIII withholding rules or the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) transfer pricing provisions. The only practical hurdles are (i) FINTRAC reporting obligations for cross-border wire transfers exceeding CAD 10,000, and (ii) the bank's internal KYC/AML screening of the underlying beneficial owners.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio into CAD for dental zirconia block export receipts. A resident CA_LP may maintain foreign currency accounts with Canadian Schedule I banks and hold USD, EUR, or RMB balances indefinitely. Compliance considerations are limited to: (i) ITA s. 95 / transfer pricing rules requiring arm's length export pricing for sales to non-resident affiliates; (ii) CRA functional currency reporting for accounts maintained in USD under ITA s. 261; and (iii) FINTRAC record-keeping for single or linked wire shipments of CAD 10,000 or more, including SWIFT MT103 narratives.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-Medium under Canadian banking law. Canada has no equivalent to the EU Electronic Money Institution (EMI) passport regime; a pure offshore digital EMI (EU/UK-licensed) cannot accept deposits or originate settlement accounts for a Canadian-resident LP without operating as, or partnering with, a deposit-taking institution regulated under the Bank Act (Canada). A foreign fintech may register as a Money Service Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and hold a money services licence in Alberta under the Consumer Protection Act (MSL), allowing remittance-style inbound/outbound wires, but MSBs are not eligible for the CA_LP's primary operational treasury accounts. Recommended structure: use a Canadian Schedule I bank as the settlement anchor and engage an FINTRAC-registered fintech only for sub-account virtual ledger management under the bank's API, not for custody of the LP's trade funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance by the General Partner's authorized signatories is effectively mandatory at most Alberta-based schedule I bank branches for a non-resident-owned LP. Remote account opening is technically permitted by the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) guidelines where enhanced due diligence (EDD) is satisfied, but in practice the major banks require an in-person interview with the General Partner's director(s) and a minimum 24% beneficial ownership disclosure. Where the GP is itself a foreign corporation without a Canadian nexus, the bank will demand: (i) original or certified true copy of the Alberta Partnership Registration (via the Corporate Registry); (ii) the complete LP agreement; and (iii) an in-branch attendance at the bank's Calgary or Edmonton commercial banking centre. Remote video acceptance is available only for supplemental limited partners holding non-voting interests below the 25% control threshold, and only after the GP has opened the account in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate General Partner with no Canadian physical footprint; identity and control ambiguity in the LP chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry Certificate of Registration for the LP; executed LP Agreement showing the GP's management authority; constitutional documents of the GP (Articles of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing); organizational chart identifying all individuals exercising 25%+ control; notarized passport scans; Canadian lawyer's tax and corporate opinion confirming the GP is not a shell entity and that the LP has substantive operations (physical plant, inventory, employees or contracted toll manufacturer in Alberta).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected international wire inflows disproportionately large relative to stated capital requirements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 3250/NAICS 339114 business plan with capital expenditure budget for CAD/CAM zirconia block production line (milling machines, sintering furnaces, raw material purchase agreements); signed purchase orders or Pro-forma invoices from equipment suppliers; pro-forma rent/lease agreement for the Alberta facility; certified capital call notice issued by the General Partner to non-resident limited partners under the LP Agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume outbound SWIFT payments to zirconia powder suppliers in jurisdictions characterized by higher AML risk (e.g., China for yttria-stabilized zirconia powder)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dual-source supplier vetting file: ISO 13485 certificates of the raw material vendors; banking KYC forms for each supplier; commercial invoices and full contract chain; Health Canada Medical Device Establishment License (MDEL) obtained under the Medical Devices Regulations SOR/98-502 evidencing legitimate trade; 12-month purchase forecasting to demonstrate that wire frequency aligns with manufacturing schedules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited Partnership pass-through structure raising tax evasion or avoidance concerns, especially where U.S. or other foreign limited partners benefit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA Form T5013 (Partnership Information Return) schedule demonstrating the LP is a valid pass-through registered partnership; US IRS Form 8832 / W-8IMY or W-8BEN-E for each non-resident partner; ITA s. 212.1 / s. 115(1) withholding analysis prepared by a cross-border tax advisor; statement confirming no capital dividend stripping; BBBA-relevant economic substance memo showing the manufacturing activity in Alberta is the source of the trade payable flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Target markets and payment rails limited to SWIFT wire and telegraphic transfer, raising counterparty and trade misinvoicing scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed dental supply distribution agreements for dental laboratory and dental implant customers; harmonized customs documentation (HS codes 9021.29, 6909.19, or 3824.99 if biocompatible ceramic compositions); certificate of analysis per zirconia block lot; anti-corruption and sanctions representation letters confirming no dealings with OFAC/EU-sanctioned end users; recorded board resolutions authorizing the specific payment rail and designated FX counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For wiring contributions to the CA_LP's Capital Escrow Account at a Canadian Schedule I bank, the following protocol applies: (i) use the bank's SWIFT/BIC direct correspondent network; (ii) include the exact beneficiary name as registered under the Alberta Corporate Registry (not abbreviated); (iii) specify the bank's branch transit and institution numbers via the SWIFT MT103 field 57A/57D; (iv) use a settlement purpose code and narrative such as 'Capital contribution to CA_LP for dental zirconia block manufacturing under LP Agreement dated [date]'—Canada has no statutory mandatory remittance-purpose code, but NBC/ATB and the major banks will route the funds internally as an inbound professional/commercial transfer; (v) for CAD amounts exceeding CAD 10,000 equivalent, the originating bank must report to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; (vi) obtain a SWIFT MT103 confirmation and a bank receipt referencing the capital call notice to complete the CRA partnership contribution record. Funds should first be held in escrow until the General Partner has issued a formal capital call, and the bank's remitting department must receive the executed LP Agreement for beneficial ownership verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for the manufacture and distribution of dental CAD/CAM zirconia blocks use (i) SWIFT MT103 for typical raw material purchases under CAD 500,000 per transaction, cleared via Payments Canada's Lynx real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system for CAD leg and via the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication for the foreign currency leg, with ISO 20022-compliant messaging; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) for large capital equipment procurement (e.g., zirconia block sintering furnaces and 5-axis milling systems) where the seller requires documentary protection—CAD/ USD clean and documentary collections may also be used to reduce cost; and (iii) CAD-denominated disbursements through the Lynx system for domestic suppliers, with the bank providing an institution-to-institution payment order referencing the invoice number. Outbound payments must carry a clear invoice reference in field 70 to avoid misrouting, and any wire over CAD 10,000 must be retained in FINTRAC CTR and EFT records. The LP should maintain a pre-clearing transaction checklist for (a) Health Canada MDEL compliance for imported raw materials, (b) Canadian Border Services Agency (CBSA) customs release numbers, and (c) letters of credit issuing bank confirmation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CAD/USD FX forwards with a Canadian Schedule I bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or bank standard FX Master Agreement, tenor up to 12 months, permitted without notional limits for covered manufacturing trade exposures

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic/illiquid currency invoicing (e.g., RMB, BRL, INR) with a Canadian bank or authorized foreign dealer, provided the underlying is a committed trade receivable/payable of the CA_LP and documentation is retained for the bank's regulatory capital treatment

Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) for long-term alignment of the LP's US-denominated dental device receivables versus CAD-denominated operating costs, subject to OSFI counterparty credit risk margin requirements for non-cleared trades

FX options (plain vanilla put/call on CAD/USD) for downside protection on zirconia block export proceeds, permissible as an over-the-counter trade with a Schedule I bank and requiring no special Bank of Canada authorization

Natural hedging via USD-denominated operating accounts and multi-currency trade sub-accounts maintained with the same Canadian bank, minimizing the volume of required forward contracts and documentary FX filings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of any change in registered office, partners, or partnership details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of $100 per day; prolonged delinquency may result in administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory requirement for independent audit; mandatory only if partnership agreement requires or if entity is designated public
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP or IFRS as specified in partnership agreement

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No mandatory annual UBO confirmation; changes in partners or beneficial ownership must be notified via Notice of Change within 15 days

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 150 - 400 annually for registered office and agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable; estimated range CAD 0 - 3,000 for any required audit services

stage_6.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Canadian Part XIII statutory rate on taxable dividends (ITA s. 212(2)); treaty-reduced to 10% (Canada-PRC DTA, ≥10% voting ownership) or 15% (portfolio); Canada-US: 5% (≥10% voting) / 15% (portfolio). Distributions from the Alberta LP to non-resident partners are not 'dividends'; active business income is taxed under Part I at the partner level with no Part XIII on distribution.
stage_6.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For any Part XIII amounts (interest, royalties, rents), the LP must obtain CRA Form NR301 from the non-resident beneficial owner before withholding at a reduced treaty rate; the CRA may verify residence via an official Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the PRC/Singapore/US tax authority. For Part I business income, treaty relief is claimed on the partner's T2 (Schedule T) or T1 annual return, supported by a TRC and the partnership agreement; the LP must also issue T5013 slips and NR4/Part XIII returns for treaty-covered payments. Alberta does not impose a separate provincial WHT.
stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: royalties — 25%; interest — 25% (non-arm's length) / exempt for arm's length interest; rents and management fees — 25%. Treaty (Canada-PRC DTA): royalties — 10%; interest — 10%. Treaty (Canada-US): royalties — 0% (arm's length patents/know-how/copyright) or 10%; interest — 0% arm's length / 15% participating interest. For IP royalties from the LP to a PRC related party, the 10% DTA rate applies to 'industrial, commercial or scientific equipment' royalties? Actually Canada-PRC royalty definition covers payments for use of patents, trademarks, designs, secret formulas, etc.: 10%. Good.
